categories.name: 技术
categories.hint: AI and the craft of software and hardware, which are one section here: models, agents, how they are built, what they can and cannot do, their effect on work; and systems, debugging, security, privacy, open source, protocols, the web platform, chips and how they are made. A war story about a database bug and a piece about what an agent can actually do both belong here. A piece that merely uses an AI tool to do something else belongs in the category of that something else. The physics or biology behind a technology is 'science'; how a tool feels to use is 'design'; a company's strategy around a technology is 'business'.

categories.name: 商业
categories.hint: Companies, strategy, markets, product decisions, platform policy, regulation of an industry. The subject is how an organisation behaves, not how a technology works. A whole economy or a government's policy is 'economy', not here.

categories.name: 投资
categories.hint: Capital and markets as the subject: asset prices, valuation, portfolio reasoning, financial theory and its failures, macro as it bears on returns. A company story is only here if it is argued from the investor's side. Labour markets, trade and public spending are 'economy'.

categories.name: 经济
categories.hint: Economics and public policy as the subject: macro, labour and jobs, immigration, trade, housing and cities, healthcare, energy, taxes, elections and how a government actually governs. The argument is about how a society allocates or rules, at the scale of a country or a city. Aimed at an investor's returns it is 'investing'; about a single company it is 'business'.

categories.name: 科学
categories.hint: Findings and methods from the natural and social sciences, read for what they show about the world: medicine, health, psychology, biology, physics, space, materials, statistics, whether a study replicates. A paper about labour markets is 'economy'; a chip fabrication process is 'tech'.

categories.name: 设计
categories.hint: Design, craft and creative work: interface and UX, typography, visual and product design, architecture as aesthetics, art, writing and the writer's process, taste and how a thing is made well. The subject is the making, not the market it sells into.

categories.name: 生活
categories.hint: How one person actually works and lives: attention, habits, tools and routines, calendars and meetings, careers, burnout, money at household scale, relationships, health as daily practice. Usually first-person and prescriptive. A study about what makes people happy is 'science'; a critique of society at large is the catch-all.

categories.name: 人文
categories.hint: LAST RESORT — use only when none of the categories above fits. History, philosophy, religion, language, media and internet culture, obituaries, how a society thinks about itself. An essay is not filed here just because it is reflective: reflective about models is still 'tech', about jobs still 'economy', about one's own working habits still 'living', about a study still 'science'.
